_comment: Authored summary targets — plan.md §9. Keyed by dataset record id. Merge with: npm --prefix api run merge:dataset
_batch: 011 — final GREY batch, closing the band gap at the ~150 target.
grey_hip-008:
**Snapshot** — 67y woman, desk job. Lower back pain for more than a year.

**Key findings**
- Pain is groin-dominant rather than back-dominant
- Hip stiffness putting on socks and getting out of a car
- Radiation stops at the buttock, left side
- No numbness, weakness or red flags
- Reports she can no longer sit through a full working day

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Groin-dominant pain with hip stiffness on dressing, and no radiation past the buttock, points away from the spine and towards the hip joint.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Internal rotation range, and whether it reproduces the groin pain
- Whether pain is worst on weight-bearing or first steps after rest
- Whether sitting itself hurts, or only getting up from sitting
- Whether squatting or sitting cross-legged has become difficult
grey_shoulder-008:
**Snapshot** — 40y woman, Ranchi. Neck pain with arm pain, 3 to 12 months.

**Key findings**
- Arm pain worse on reaching overhead
- Pain stays above the elbow, at the right shoulder only
- No hand numbness, no grip loss, no dexterity change
- Working with difficulty; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Overhead-provoked arm pain that stops above the elbow, with no hand symptoms, points to the shoulder joint rather than a cervical root.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Painful arc, and whether passive movement hurts as much as active
- Impingement tests and rotator cuff power
- Whether the pain wakes her lying on that side
- Whether neck movement changes the arm pain at all
grey_vascular-004:
**Snapshot** — 58y man, Surat. Leg pain and difficulty walking, 3 to 12 months.

**Key findings**
- Walking limited to 100–500 metres, both legs
- Pain settles on standing still alone — no need to sit or bend
- Diabetes and tobacco use
- Radiation stops at the buttock; no numbness or weakness
- No red flags

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Relief on standing still, without flexion, is the discriminator separating this from spinal claudication. With diabetes and smoking alongside, a vascular cause is the stronger query.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Peripheral pulses and ankle-brachial index
- Whether the claudication distance is consistent day to day
- Any rest pain, night pain in the foot, or slow-healing ulcers
- Smoking history in pack-years, and whether he has tried to stop
grey_inflammatory-004:
**Snapshot** — 31y man, student. Lower back pain for 3 to 12 months.

**Key findings**
- Morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes
- Pain improves with movement and worsens with rest
- Sleep disturbed sometimes
- No radiation, numbness, weakness or red flags
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Prolonged morning stiffness with exercise-responsive pain, at 31 with months of symptoms, fits an inflammatory rather than mechanical pattern.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Alternating buttock pain, or heel and chest wall pain
- Family or personal history of psoriasis, uveitis or inflammatory bowel disease
- Which anti-inflammatory and at what dose — a dramatic response supports the pattern
- Whether pain wakes him in the second half of the night
grey_widespread-004:
**Snapshot** — 34y woman, desk job. Lower back pain for more than a year.

**Key findings**
- Pain in many parts of the body with constant tiredness
- Sleep disturbed most nights
- The back pain itself has no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Walking unrestricted; managing daily tasks independently
- Painkillers giving partial relief only

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Widespread pain with persistent fatigue and no localising spinal findings suggests the back pain is one part of a broader picture.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Which other sites hurt, and whether they preceded the back pain
- Sleep quality separately from pain — unrefreshing sleep is part of the pattern
- Mood, concentration, and how long the fatigue has run
- She wrote *(translated)*: "The medicine gives some relief but the pain does not go completely."
grey_unclear-004:
**Snapshot** — 29y man, driver. Selected "none of these" as the main complaint, so the questionnaire never showed the spine branches.

**Key findings**
- No spinal complaint selected
- All ten red-flag questions answered no
- No other medical conditions reported
- The back, neck, function and treatment sections were never reached
- There is no symptom detail on file to review

**Supporting the triage verdict** — The complaint does not match any spine pattern the questionnaire can route on. This is a gap in the intake rather than a clinical finding.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What the problem actually is, in his own words
- Whether "none of these" was genuine or the option list did not fit
- Whether the referral was for something the form does not cover
- Whether it is worth re-taking the form once the complaint is clear
